payload.name: Preserve explicit evaluative descriptors in extraction
payload.description: When a speaker directly evaluates a specific entity, event, or person with a concrete descriptor (e.g., 'looks great', 'is beautiful'), preserve that descriptor in extracted memory content instead of replacing it with a general emotion like excitement or pride.
content: During candidate extraction, when a message contains a direct evaluative statement about a specific entity, event, or person (e.g., '[thing] looks/feels/seems [descriptor]'), include that exact descriptor as a distinct fact in the candidate content.
Do not replace the descriptor with a general emotional summary (e.g., 'excitement', 'pride', 'support'); retain both the specific evaluation and the surrounding context.
When updating an existing memory, ensure the specific descriptive fact is added even if the update also captures broader sentiments or relationship dynamics.

solves: Extraction candidates often paraphrase a speaker's direct evaluation of a specific entity (e.g., 'the studio looks great') into a general sentiment like 'excitement' or 'pride', losing the concrete descriptor. This skill instructs extractors to preserve explicit descriptive adjectives or qualifiers when candidates are generated or updated, so future questions about those specific descriptions can be answered. It applies to any conversation where a person directly evaluates an entity, event, or person; it does not apply to inferred sentiments or non-evaluative factual statements.
